proof_summary: A continuant invariant and a congruence modulo \(5n-4\) yield \(a(n)=(5n-4)/\gcd(5n-4,3\cdot4\cdots n)\). For each residue of \(p\bmod 5\), one chooses \(c\in\{1,2,3,4\}\) and \(n=(cp+4)/5<p\) (with \(p=11\) handled at \(n=3\)); conversely, the product formula forces every occurrence to satisfy \(5n-4=cp\), \(1\le c<5\), and \(n<p\), so the residue modulo \(5\) determines \(c\) and then \(n\) uniquely.
